plainEnglishByLine.invocation: My Mother, Mother of the true sacred flames, You are eternally victorious.
plainEnglishByLine.refrain: I have grabbed onto the hem of Your garment; I have no one else.
plainEnglishByLine.v1a: My breath is going to abandon me.
plainEnglishByLine.v1b: Then You will cry out — and I will not turn back.
plainEnglishByLine.v2a: What is there to get from this life anyway, Mother?
plainEnglishByLine.v2b: If I do not get to see You, what will I gain from living?
plainEnglishByLine.v3a: I will come to Your door.
plainEnglishByLine.v3b: Even if You have me swear by Your own oath, I will never leave You.
plainEnglishByLine.v4b: Who knows when the final turn will come? This body is a heap of earth.
plainEnglishByLine.v5a: I will just stay at Your feet.
plainEnglishByLine.v5b: You forgive me, and I will bear it with a smile.
plainEnglishByLine.v6a: I will come as Yours, Mother.
plainEnglishByLine.v6b: Even You will cry then, if I ever left You.
plainEnglishByLine.v7b: Show me happiness, Mother. Otherwise, tears are plentiful.
plainEnglishByLine.v8a: Even then, I will say nothing, Mother.
plainEnglishByLine.v8b: Just tell me once, before whom will I unburden my sorrows?
plainEnglishByLine.outro1: Writing this, I will leave, Mother:
plainEnglishByLine.outro2: Even in the next life, Mother, I will be called Your son.

plainEnglishByLine.line-000: To offer this wedding garland of letters, worthy of the bridegroom Aruṇācala,
plainEnglishByLine.line-001: O Gaṇapati, treasure of compassion, lend Your gracious hand and protect me!
plainEnglishByLine.line-002: Aruṇācala Śiva, Aruṇācala Śiva, Aruṇācala Śiva, Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-003: You uproot the ego of those who think 'Aruṇācala' within the heart itself, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-004: Like aḻaku and sundaram—both “beauty”—may I and You unite and remain inseparably one, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-005: You entered my heart, drew me in, and kept me captive in Your heart’s cave—what is this, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-006: For whose sake did You claim me? If You cast me off, the world will reproach You, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-007: Escape this blame! Why did You make me remember You? Now, who can let go, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-008: O You whose grace exceeds that of the mother who bore me, is this Your grace, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-009: Remain firmly upon my mind, so that it cannot run away, deceiving You, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-010: Show Your beauty, so that, seeing You, I may grow still, with no room left for wandering, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-011: Having destroyed me now, if You do not merge with me, is this manliness, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-012: Why this slumber while others drag me away? Is this befitting You, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-013: When the five sense-thieves enter my heart, are You not there within, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-014: Who could enter unseen by You, the One alone? This is Your own trick, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-015: O meaning of Oṃ, without equal or superior, who can know You, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-016: Like a mother, giving me Your grace and taking charge of me is Your duty, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-017: As the Eye of the eye, seeing without eyes, who can see You? See me, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-018: Draw me as a magnet draws iron, never let me go, and remain united with me, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-019: O Ocean of grace who took the form of a mountain, bestow Your grace abundantly, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-020: O Gem of resplendent light shining below, above, and everywhere, destroy my baseness, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-021: Shining as the teacher, root out all my faults, make me virtuous, and take charge of me, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-022: Keep me from falling into the cruelty of women with sharp sword-like eyes; in abundant grace, unite with me, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-023: Though I plead, like a deceiver You show no pity at all. Say “Do not fear,” and grant Your grace, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-024: Do not bring blemish upon Your flawless fame of giving unasked; bestow Your grace, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-025: O fruit in my hand, grant that I may drink the juice of Your true being and become drunk with joy, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-026: Hoisting a banner, You slay Your devotees; embracing You, how shall I live, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-027: O You whose nature is free of wrath, what fault did I commit that You take me as Your target, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-028: O great mountain of compassion, praised by Gautama, cast Your sidelong glance on me and take charge of me, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-029: O radiant sun that swallows everything, make the lotus of my mind blossom, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-030: Seeking food, I turn to You; becoming food myself, I shall pass into peace, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-031: Lay Your ray-like hands on me to cool my mind, and open the nectar-mouth, O moon of grace, Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-032: Strip away my covering, leave me bare, and graciously grant Your glory, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-033: Be united with me there in stillness, so that the ocean of bliss surges and speech and thought subside, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-034: Without testing me anymore by playing tricks, show Your form of light, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-035: Free me from the delusion of this world, from learning the arts of deception, and show me the art of abiding as I truly am, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-036: If You do not unite with me, my body will melt into water, and I shall perish in a river of tears, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-037: If You reject me with “Away!”, my deeds will burn me. Tell me, what other way of escape is there, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-038: Without speaking, You said, “Remain without speech,” and You stayed utterly still, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-039: Aruṇācala Śiva, Aruṇācala Śiva, Aruṇācala Śiva, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-040: If You sleep in stillness, like an idler, enjoying bliss, tell me, what other fate is left to me, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-041: You showed prowess; deeming all deceit destroyed, you remained unmoving, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-042: I am worse than a dog; with what strength could I seek and reach You, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-043: Without knowledge, I long for You and grow weary. Graciously reveal true knowledge and end this weariness, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-044: Like a bee, You too stood before me, saying, “You have not blossomed.” Why, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-045: You took possession of me, a flawed one who did not know truth. What a principle this is, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-046: The Self itself is reality. You Yourself reveal this, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-047: You said, “Turn inward; each day look with the inner eye at the ‘I’, and it will become clear,” O my Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-048: I sought You with a mind that lacked courage, and turned back. Grant Your grace, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-049: What use is this birth without knowledge through inquiry? Come and make it worthy, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-050: Grant that I may merge in Your true self, where those pure in mind and speech merge, O my Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-051: Taking You as God, I came for refuge to You, and You wiped me out completely, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-052: O good treasure of sacred grace, found without seeking, graciously dispel my heart’s confusion, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-053: When I boldly sought Your true inner realm, I was shattered; bestow grace, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-054: If You do not touch me with Your gracious hand and embrace my body, I shall be lost. Grant Your grace, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-055: You who are free of fault, unite with my heart and grant that joy may abide forever, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-056: There is no room for mockery. Look upon me, who sought You, with Your gracious smile, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-057: You had no shyness! When I sought You, You united with me as my very self and stood unmoving as a pillar, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-058: Before Your fire burns me to ashes, pour down the rain of sweet grace, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-059: Unite with me so that “You” and “I” cease. Grant the state of abiding forever full of joy, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-060: When will the waves of thought cease, so that I may unite with You, whose form is subtle space, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-061: Graciously cut away my deluded understanding; I am a fool unacquainted with scriptural learning, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-062: As I, softening and melting again and again, entered to seek refuge in You, You stood naked, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-063: You awakened longing for You in me, who had no love. Do not disappoint me; grant Your grace, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-064: A fruit that wastes away and rots is of no use. It is good to seek it out and eat it while it is ripe, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-065: If You do not take me and give Yourself so that I do not suffer, You are Death itself to me, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-066: Having made me ripe by Your gaze, Your thought, and Your touch upon my body, graciously take me as Your own, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-067: Before the poison of delusion seizes me, reaches my head and kills me, grant that Your grace may take hold of me, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-068: Look on me with grace and end my delusion. If You will not look, who can tell You, “Look with grace”? O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-069: You removed my madness and made me a madman like You. Grant the medicine to cure this madness, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-070: Unite with me, who in fear has sought You, the fearless one. Why should You fear, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-071: Tell what is petty knowledge! Tell what is noble knowledge! Bestow grace that we may embrace, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-072: Grant me complete union, so that the mind, steeped in earthly scent, may take on perfect fragrance, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-073: The very moment I thought of Your name, You seized and drew me. Who can know Your greatness, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-074: To drive out my ghostly nature, You possessed me as a ghost that will not leave, and made me one possessed. What a wonder, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-075: So that I, who am a tender green vine, do not wither without support, protect me as a supporting stake, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-076: Bewitching me with powder and snatching away my awareness, You revealed Your awareness, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-077: Graciously show the battle-play of grace in the common expanse where there is no going or coming, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-078: Grant that, having relinquished attachment to the material body, I may behold and unite with Your splendor always, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-079: O Aruṇācala, You shine as the healing mountain of grace. Why hesitate to give the cure for bewilderment?
plainEnglishByLine.line-080: Destroying the attachment of those who approach You with attachment, shine free of attachment, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-081: I have little understanding: when overwhelmed, I plead. Without deceiving me, grant me Your grace, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-082: Protect me with grace, lest I become a ship tossed by a great storm without a helmsman, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-083: Having untied the knot whose beginning and end are unknown, is it not Your duty, like a mother, to place me in the final goal, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-084: Instead of being like a mirror held before a noseless man, graciously lift and embrace me, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-085: Grant that we may unite as reality on the soft flower-bed of the mind within the house of the body, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-086: By uniting with tender-natured devotees who are more and more humble, You have attained greatness—what a wonder, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-087: Removing my dense delusion with the eye-salve of Your grace, You brought me under the sway of Your Reality, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-088: Having shaved me bare, You danced in the open expanse. What a wonder, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-089: Dispelling my desire and making me desirous of You, fulfil my desire, my Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-090: If you remain as a silent one like a stone without blossoming, can this be silence, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-091: Who put dirt in my mouth and ruined my livelihood, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-092: Who bewitched my mind and stole it away without anyone knowing, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-093: I called You “Ramaṇa,” my beloved. Do not take offense; come and make me rejoice, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-094: In the abode of the empty expanse where there is no night and day, come, let us rejoice, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-095: You took aim and fired the arrow of grace; You devoured me together with my life-breath, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-096: You are the gain. What have You gained by gaining me, who has gained nothing here or hereafter, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-097: Did You not tell me to come? Come and measure out my portion. The trouble of doing so is Your fate, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-098: Saying “Come,” You entered my heart and bestowed Your life; at that very moment I lost my life. Such grace, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-099: To let go is misery; grant grace that I may give up life without letting go of you, O Aruṇācala!
plainEnglishByLine.line-100: You drew me out of home, stealthily entered the home of my heart, and revealed Your home. Such grace, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-101: I have disclosed Your deeds. Do not resent me; openly reveal Your grace and protect me, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-102: Grant me the reality of the Vedas, shining without another in Vedānta itself, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-103: Take my reproach as praise; keep me in Your household of grace, and graciously never forsake me, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-104: Graciously dissolve me into love in You, love embodied, like a hailstone in water, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-105: The moment I thought “Aruṇai,” I was caught in the snare of grace. Could Your net of grace ever fail, O Aruṇācala?
plainEnglishByLine.line-106: Having resolved to catch me in grace, like a spider You bound me, imprisoned and devoured me, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-107: Grant that I may love the devotees of the devotees who hear Your name with love, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-108: May You graciously live forever, protecting helpless ones like me so that they experience bliss, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-109: Let Your ears, which hear the sweet words of devotees whose very bones melt with love, receive my poor words too, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-110: O mountain of patience, graciously bear with my poor words as fine words; then do as You wish, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-111: You have given Your garland; O Aruṇācala Ramaṇa, graciously wear my garland, O Aruṇācala.
plainEnglishByLine.line-113: May the loving devotees flourish also!
plainEnglishByLine.line-114: May the Marital Garland of Letters flourish!
